findings.title: Cleanup registers a literal "alias" instead of the created IDP alias
findings.body: The cleanup `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` uses the literal string "alias" rather than the alias of the IDP just created. The cleanup therefore never removes the `idp-alias-N` providers, so they leak into other tests in the same realm. The same copy-paste pattern also appears at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`. The method reference should capture the actual alias.

findings.title: remove() now always loads the IDP from the database
findings.body: `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is executed unconditionally at the top of `remove()`. Previously the DB lookup only happened when the alias key was invalidated, and the cache path avoided it entirely. Every IDP removal now incurs an extra uncached DB query, even when the cached entry is present and could supply the same data for the login-invalidation check.

findings.title: getForLogin Javadoc does not describe the new public-broker requirement
findings.body: The change adds `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || BROKER_PUBLIC` to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()`, so an org-linked IDP now qualifies for login only if it is marked broker-public. The Javadoc for `getForLogin` (lines 150-158) still says an IDP is usable for login if it is enabled, not link-only, and not hidden on login. It omits this new condition, which callers and maintainers will need to know.
